outbreaks.title: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) — DRC / Uganda
outbreaks.status: PHEIC · Active — regional risk assessed HIGH
outbreaks.desc: As of 20 August 2026 (data to 19 Aug), DRC has reported 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths, with 837 patients currently hospitalised in isolation — an increase of 81 cases and 40 deaths in a single day, concentrated in Ituri (56), North Kivu (18), and Haut-Uele (7). With more confirmed cases than the 2018–2020 outbreak (3,317 cases), this is now the largest Ebola outbreak ever documented in DRC, and per the WHO Director-General's own 18 August remarks, the second-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded worldwide — moving faster than any previous Ebola outbreak. A second IHR Emergency Committee met 18 August 2026 and issued updated, more detailed temporary recommendations (surveillance, case investigation, infection control, and — new — social measures/mass gatherings/domestic mobility guidance); the Committee did not lift the PHEIC. WHO/AFRO assessed regional risk as 'High' as of 14 August 2026.
outbreaks.more: For the first time, two vaccines designed specifically against Bundibugyo virus have entered human trials; a third, cross-protective vaccine is moving toward a phase 3 trial after animal-study success. The WHO-sponsored PARTNERS treatment trial has enrolled 100 patients — no vaccine or treatment is yet approved. Temporary recommendations now extend to Angola, Burundi, CAR, Republic of Congo, Rwanda, and South Sudan in addition to DRC and Uganda. Imported-case status: France's case (24 Jun) has shown no secondary transmission (41 days post-discharge as of 14 Aug); Uganda's most recent imported case was discharged 16 Jul, with 42-day enhanced monitoring ending 27 Aug; two DRC-diagnosed cases have been treated in Germany. WHO DG's 18 Aug remarks stressed the epidemic is 'far from being under control' and is being fuelled by insecurity, displacement, and population movement along roads, rivers, and mining routes, with many deaths occurring at home, outside treatment centres and known contact lists.
outbreaks.src: WHO DON-2026-DON615 (1 Aug 2026); WHO 2nd IHR Emergency Committee temporary recommendations (24 Aug 2026 posting, meeting held 18 Aug); WHO DG opening remarks, 18 Aug 2026; ECDC Ebola outbreak update, 20 Aug 2026

outbreaks.title: Broader Transmission of Mpox (Clade Ib MPXV) — Global Situation
outbreaks.desc: WHO global situation update on the wider geographic spread of clade Ib mpox virus, preceding the Feb 2026 report of a clade Ib/IIb recombinant strain.

outbreaks.title: Infant Formula Contaminated with Cereulide Toxin — Multi-country
outbreaks.desc: WHO international food safety event notification: infant formula and products containing arachidonic acid oil found contaminated with cereulide toxin (produced by Bacillus cereus), affecting multiple countries.

outbreaks.title: Andes Hantavirus — Cruise Ship (M/V Hondius), Multi-country
outbreaks.desc: Fifth and reportedly final DON on this cluster. Following notification 2 May of severe acute respiratory illness aboard, 13 cases confirmed/probable across passengers and crew (147 aboard), including 3 deaths (23% CFR). A probable case in Tristan da Cunha was later lab-confirmed after disembarkation.
outbreaks.more: CDC assessed overall US public risk as extremely low throughout; coordination extended to State Department travel guidance for affected Americans.

outbreaks.title: Marburg Virus Disease — Ethiopia (closed)
outbreaks.desc: Outbreak declared over after two incubation periods (42 days) with no new cases. Final tally: 19 cases (14 confirmed, 5 probable), 14 deaths. 857 contacts completed monitoring. An earlier DON on the same outbreak was issued 21 Nov 2025.

outbreaks.title: Mpox — Recombinant Clade Ib/IIb Virus, Global
outbreaks.desc: WHO DON flags a recombinant mpox virus carrying genomic elements of both clade Ib and clade IIb — a genetic-mixing signal of concern for surveillance systems tracking lineage-specific countermeasures.

outbreaks.title: Nipah Virus — Bangladesh
outbreaks.desc: Seasonal Nipah reporting period; date-palm-sap transmission remains the primary route under investigation.

governance.title: OpenAI "Biodefense in the Intelligence Age" action plan
governance.desc: An action plan for AI-powered biological resilience, published alongside OpenAI's own biodefense summit — positions frontier labs as active participants in defensive biosecurity infrastructure, not just sources of dual-use risk.

governance.title: US Policy for Stopping High-Risk Life Sciences Research
governance.desc: Prohibits federally funded dangerous gain-of-function (DGOF) research and establishes new review requirements for potential DGOF research and international research of concern (IROC). Supersedes an earlier DURC/PEPP policy consolidation before it took effect.

governance.title: Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act (S.3741) introduced
governance.desc: Introduced in the US Senate; read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

governance.title: IBBIS International Standards Initiative launched (Singapore)
governance.desc: Meeting convened stakeholders from industry, government, academia and standards bodies to push consistent global adoption of DNA synthesis screening.

governance.title: Executive Order 14292
governance.desc: Directs revision or replacement of the 2024 OSTP nucleic-acid synthesis screening framework.

governance.title: OSTP Screening Framework takes effect for purchases
governance.desc: Nucleic acid synthesis screening becomes a live requirement for purchases (condition of federal life-sciences research funding).

governance.title: OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening issued
governance.desc: Established as a voluntary-turned-conditional requirement tied to federal life-sciences funding eligibility.

governance.title: IBBIS Common Mechanism launched
governance.desc: Free, open-source, globally available DNA/RNA synthesis screening software released.

governance.title: IBBIS founded as independent Swiss foundation
governance.desc: Incubated out of NTI | bio; headquartered Geneva.

governance.title: HHS voluntary synthesis-screening guidance
governance.desc: Baseline (non-binding) starting point for US gene-synthesis screening policy.
